name: Microsoft Copilot
scope: The updated Microsoft Copilot app (web, desktop and mobile) used with a personal Microsoft account. Microsoft says its older app follows a separate FAQ, and that work and school accounts follow different terms.

activity.title: Microsoft Copilot for individuals: your activity history

controls.title: Microsoft Copilot for individuals: your privacy controls and choices

state.title: U.S. State Data Privacy Laws Notice

training.summary: Microsoft says prompts, responses and file contents in the Copilot app are not used to train foundation models.

evidence.quote: Prompts, responses, and your file contents when using the Microsoft Copilot app aren't used to train foundation models.
We don't use this feedback to train the foundation models used by Copilot.
Microsoft Copilot also uses prompts and related data to provide and improve services, including relevant advertising.

training.note: Microsoft's statement is about foundation models. Its privacy statement separately says prompts and related data are used to provide and improve services.

retention.summary: Microsoft says Copilot keeps your prior conversations so you can return to them. The documents we read for the updated app state no retention period.

evidence.quote: Microsoft Copilot keeps your prior conversations with Copilot so you can revisit them or continue them at any time.

deletion.summary: Microsoft says you can delete single conversations in the app and your whole history in its privacy dashboard. The documents we read do not state how long removal takes.

evidence.quote: To delete individual conversations from your chat history:
To delete your entire Copilot chat history, see Manage your Copilot activity history in the privacy dashboard.

human_review.summary: Microsoft says people may review Copilot conversations for safety, legal, product improvement or troubleshooting purposes.

evidence.quote: Humans may review your conversations in Copilot for safety, legal, product improvement, or troubleshooting.

ads_sale.summary: Microsoft says it does not sell personal information. It says Copilot may show ads to users without a Microsoft 365 subscription, and that personalized ads might use your chat history. A setting turns ad personalization off.

evidence.quote: As noted above, we do not sell personal information
If you use Microsoft Copilot and don’t have a Microsoft 365 subscription, you might see advertising in Copilot.
Personalized ads might use your chat history, saved memories, and other Microsoft data you've chosen to share to tailor ads and offers to your interests over time.
Regardless of your settings, Copilot doesn’t show personalized advertising to users under the age of 18.

private_mode.summary: The documents we read for the updated Copilot app describe no temporary or no-history chat mode.

transparency.summary: The privacy statement shows when it was last updated and points to a change history page.

evidence.quote: When we post changes to this statement, we will revise the "last updated" date at the top of the statement and describe the changes on the Change history page.

business.summary: Microsoft says these pages do not apply to work, school or organizational accounts.

evidence.quote: This article does not apply when you sign in to the Microsoft Copilot app or use Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps with a work, school, or organizational (Microsoft Entra) account.

age.summary: At least 13, or older in some countries and regions.

evidence.quote: You must be at least 13 years old to use Copilot, and in some countries or regions, the minimum age may be higher depending on regional requirements.

opt_out.summary: Microsoft says chats in the updated app are not used to train foundation models, so there is no training setting to change. You can turn off ad personalization.
steps: Open Microsoft Copilot and sign in with your Microsoft account.

evidence.quote: Turn off the Allow ads personalization toggle.
Generic ads are selected based on the most recent content of your current conversation and don’t use your past chat history.

caveats: With personalization off, Microsoft says generic ads are still selected from the most recent content of your current conversation.
